sources.entry: Linked Ideas - macOS application to write down and connect ideas.

summary.one_liner: Linked Ideas is a macOS app for free-form note taking, where you place ideas on a canvas and connect them with links, plus a companion iOS app for reading documents.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you add concepts (idea boxes) anywhere on a free-form canvas, then add, edit and remove links between them, with optional text explanations on each link. Concepts can be formatted with strikethrough, bold, seven predefined colors and font size changes via keyboard shortcuts. Groups of selected concepts can be aligned (vertical left, horizontal center, equal vertical spacing). The whole document can be zoomed and panned. The README says documents can be stored in iCloud and shared across multiple computers. Unlike tree-based mind mapping tools, it allows loops and multiple groups of ideas without a predefined hierarchy.
use_cases: connecting related ideas in a non-hierarchical way
mind mapping without a tree structure
syncing idea documents across Macs via iCloud
notable: Free-form canvas with no required top-down hierarchy, so loops and multiple idea groups are allowed
Keyboard shortcuts for strikethrough, bold, seven quick colors and font sizing
Alignment and equal-spacing tools for groups of concepts
Documents stored in iCloud and shareable across computers
caveats: README gives no install or build instructions and no explicit platform requirements beyond macOS and iOS
Development roadmap is pointed to external GitHub project and notes links, which were left empty in the README
